left: placement accuracy by how short the child is. right: the three conditions, no help, plus the formula, plus the CDC values for that age. 6 of 13 models shown, 40 children each.

the same 40 children, 16 of them truly below −2. dark: a short child placed above the line, a missed referral. light: a child placed below it, an unneeded one. the CDC values fix most models, but Qwen2.5 72B trades 16 misses for 13 unneeded referrals: the error changes direction instead of going away.
green: asked for the CDC median height at an age, accurate to about a centimetre. red: asked to place a specific child with no reference given.

the family-facing chart for the Turner syndrome teaching case. the dashed line marks the visit where height fell below −2 SD, and the note underneath explains it in plain language and points the family back to their clinician.

the sample patient's height and weight from the record, with flagged points marked. below, height velocity between visits: the early jumps of 48 and 23 cm a year are flagged as likely measurement artifacts, so a bad entry is caught before it reads as a growth problem.

the pipeline: collect 14,088 items, label each condition and its role with a local model, map names to ICD-10-CM through the official Alphabetic Index, check with two other models, then publish a searchable explorer.
tested conditions by ICD-10-CM chapter, stacked by benchmark. every chapter is covered, but unevenly: external causes of morbidity has fewer than ten items.
share of healthy short children each model refers. same children, same question, opposite behaviour.
the percentile at which each model starts flagging. there is no shared threshold.
the same models after one clinical sentence is added to the prompt.
what the referrals cost, in one picture: healthy children worked up for each child with a real disorder, worst model against best.

Medicare inpatient stays in eight Stroke Belt states, drawn from the patient's home county to the hospital's county. Arcs run light at home to deep at the hospital, so each starburst is a hub the surrounding counties depend on. Rings are the 47 rural hospitals here that closed since 2010 and could be placed on the map. Open it to tilt the map, hover any arc, county or closure, and filter out small flows.
citation impact climbs with each added involvement signal. left: impact by index score, medians marked on a log scale. right: the same papers as NIH citation percentiles.
a sample of abstracts laid out by topic, coloured by index score. involved papers bunch on one side of the map, so topic is a confounder the control sets have to absorb.
share of papers above each citation level, log scale. half of the papers with two or more signals beat the field average (RCR 1.0), against 37% of controls.
each signal alone against the population baseline. red signals are structural and predict impact; the grey ones are framing and predict nothing.
the same breakdown against controls matched on disease heading. the structural signals stay on top.
after matching on year and team size. the dashed lines are each group's median; the involved group's sits to the right.
a second matched comparison: involved papers against matched papers from the same search that scored zero, so both groups come out of one retrieval.
the tightest topic control: each involved paper paired with the zero-score paper whose abstract embedding sits closest. a much smaller sample.
the comparison repeated inside each of 18 journals. 13 point the same way.
within broad disease groups against disease-matched controls. most groups favour involved papers; mental and metabolic disorders do not.
the same question with a stricter control pool, heading-matched controls pooled per disease group. the gains shrink and three groups hold.
specific disease headings with at least 50 controls, top 15 by effect. COVID-19, HIV and pain survive false-discovery correction.
one thing the index does not predict: early citation speed. involved papers are cited more slowly in their first two years until three or more signals.

share of trial sites in the United States, by start year, for trials cited as evidence in PharmGKB gene–drug relationships. colour is the number of trials that year. the US share falls from around half in the late 2000s to a fifth or less after 2016.

the seven sugar modifications in the training data, drawn in ChemDraw for the paper, each shown against the unmodified ribose position it replaces (grey marks the change). backbone modifications such as phosphorothioate are not part of this set.

how often each modification appears across the training siRNAs, in the same order as the structures above. 2′-O-methyl and 2′-fluoro dominate; the rarer chemistries give the model very few examples to learn from.
feature weights from the trained model. read with the co-occurrence caveat above.
